title: Underived tensor projection for closed pro-etale immersions with arbitrary ring coefficients
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings and put $R_Z=i^{-1}R$. Use the module inverse/direct images of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image, lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] and ordinary sheaf tensor products [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For every $R_Z$-module sheaf $M$ and $R$-module sheaf $F$, the canonical projection map
$$\pi_{M,F}:(i_*M)\otimes_R F\longrightarrow i_*(M\otimes_{R_Z}i^{-1}F)$$
is an isomorphism, natural in both inputs. Here $\pi_{M,F}$ is the $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$-adjunct of the map
$$i^{-1}((i_*M)\otimes_R F)\cong i^{-1}i_*M\otimes_{R_Z}i^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_M\otimes1}M\otimes_{R_Z}i^{-1}F,$$
where the first arrow is the ordinary inverse-image tensor comparison of [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] and $\varepsilon$ is the adjunction counit. If $R\to B$ is a morphism of commutative ring sheaves and $F=B$, this is an isomorphism of $B$-module sheaves, using the action on the $B$ tensor factor and the direct-image action through $B\to i_*i^{-1}B$. No flatness, finite presentation or constructibility assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tags 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion) and 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), together with sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback). Agent-formulated underived projection consequence, not a projection theorem stated in these tags or in Bhatt-Scholze 6.8.13.

proof.text: Put $H=(i_*M)\otimes_R F$ and $N=M\otimes_{R_Z}i^{-1}F$. Write $\sigma^i$ for the inverse-image tensor comparison. The closed counit $\varepsilon_M:i^{-1}i_*M\to M$ of the module adjunction $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$ of the ringed open-closed lemma is invertible by the closed-counit lemma, which states this for every adjunction between the actual module inverse image and the direct image with action through the inverse-image ring unit (the ringed open-closed lemma itself only records an abstract isomorphism $i^{-1}i_*\cong\operatorname{id}$). Hence $\alpha=(\varepsilon_M\otimes1)\circ\sigma^i_{i_*M,F}:i^{-1}H\to N$ is invertible: its inverse is $(\sigma^i_{i_*M,F})^{-1}\circ(\varepsilon_M^{-1}\otimes1)$. The adjunction formula for the transpose gives $\pi_{M,F}=i_*(\alpha)\circ\eta_H$, where $\eta_H:H\to i_*i^{-1}H$ is the closed unit. This is precisely the adjunct specified in the statement.

source.place: Tag 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), closed counit; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); agent-written adjunct formula

proof.text: Apply the tensor comparison to $j$ and use the open-closed vanishing: $j^{-1}H\cong(j^{-1}i_*M)\otimes_{j^{-1}R}j^{-1}F=0$. Here tensoring the zero sheaf gives zero directly from the sheafified sectionwise tensor definition, since every pure tensor with a zero entry is zero. Apply the ringed localization sequence to the $R$-module sheaf $H$: $0\to j_!j^{-1}H\to H\xrightarrow{\eta_H}i_*i^{-1}H\to0$. Its first nonzero term is zero (extension by zero of the zero presheaf is zero), so exactness says that $\eta_H$ is an isomorphism. The quasi-compactness hypothesis required for this sequence is exactly the hypothesis on $j$ in the item.

The formula of step 1 expresses $\pi_{M,F}$ as the composite of the isomorphism $\eta_H$ from step 2 and the functorial image $i_*(\alpha)$ of an isomorphism. Its inverse is $\eta_H^{-1}\circ i_*(\alpha^{-1})$. Naturality in $M$ and $F$ follows by substituting the naturality equations for $\sigma^i$, $\varepsilon$ and $\eta$ into this formula: for $a:M\to M\prime$ and $b:F\to F\prime$, one obtains $i_*(a\otimes i^{-1}b)\circ\pi_{M,F}=\pi_{M\prime,F\prime}\circ(i_*a\otimes b)$. All these are the actual adjunction and tensor maps, so this proves naturality of the specified projection map.

source.place: Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), functoriality; agent-written composition and inverse calculation

proof.text: For the coefficient clause take $F=B$. On $V\to X$, write $V_Z=Z\times_XV$ and $m\in(i_*M)(V)=M(V_Z)$. If $b\in B(V)$, let $\bar b\in(i^{-1}B)(V_Z)$ be its image under the inverse-image unit. The pure-tensor characterization of $\sigma^i$, followed by the counit and the adjunction triangle identity, makes the composite in step 1 send $m\otimes b$ to $m\otimes\bar b$. Thus for $c\in B(V)$ its value on $m\otimes cb$ is $m\otimes\overline{cb}=m\otimes\bar c\bar b=\bar c(m\otimes\bar b)$, exactly the asserted direct-image $B$-action through $B\to i_*i^{-1}B$. The equality extends additively and through sheafification because sheaf tensor products are sheafifications of sectionwise tensors: locally their sections are sums of pure tensors. Hence $\pi_{M,B}$ is $B$-linear. Its already constructed inverse is $B$-linear as well: apply $\pi_{M,B}$ to both sides of $\pi_{M,B}^{-1}(cy)=c\pi_{M,B}^{-1}(y)$ and use injectivity. This proves the isomorphism in $B$-modules without imposing any condition on $R\to B$.

lean.statement: theorem closed_underived_projection {X Z : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion i] (U : X.ProEt) [IsOpenImmersion U.hom] [QuasiCompact U.hom] (hU : Set.range U.hom = (Set.range i)ᶜ) (R : Rings X) : (∀ (M : Modules (inverseRing i R)) (F : Modules R), IsIso (projection i R M F)) ∧ (∀ (M M' : Modules (inverseRing i R)) (F F' : Modules R) (a : M ⟶ M') (b : F ⟶ F'), tensorMap ((proEtaleRingedDirectImage i R).map a) b ≫ projection i R M' F' = projection i R M F ≫ (proEtaleRingedDirectImage i R).map (tensorMap a ((inverse i R).map b))) ∧ (∀ (M : Modules (inverseRing i R)) (B : Rings X) (a : R ⟶ B), CoefficientLinear i R M B a)
lean.note: The adjunction data are uniquely fixed by equality of their unit with the recorded actual inverseSection, not selected from mere existence. The projection is the precise tensor-comparison/counit adjunct. The coefficient clause fixes B-actions by pure tensors and requires the B-linear isomorphism to have exactly this underlying projection; no arbitrary comparison is substituted.
